summary: San Francisco punk band led by Jello Biafra, known for sharp political satire set to fast, surf-tinged guitar. They were among the most influential American hardcore bands and helped build the scene's independent infrastructure.
know: East Bay Ray's reverb-heavy guitar borrowed from 1960s surf music.
Jello Biafra founded the Alternative Tentacles label in 1979.
Biafra ran for mayor of San Francisco in 1979 and finished fourth.

influencedBy.why: Biafra has described seeing the Ramones in 1977 as the push that drew him into punk.
Biafra is a longtime Stooges devotee, and their raw attack shaped the band's early sound.
The Pistols showed how punk could be confrontational and openly political.
The MC5's mix of loud rock and radical politics prefigured the Dead Kennedys' approach.

influenced.why: Napalm Death recorded a Dead Kennedys cover, carrying their politics into grindcore.
NOFX built on the Dead Kennedys' blend of fast punk and satirical humor.
Bay Area punk that followed, including Green Day, grew up in a scene the Dead Kennedys helped define.

cousins.why: Both used noisy, urgent music as a vehicle for blunt political commentary.
Same fusion of aggressive music and pointed political message.

summary: One of the first British punk bands, the Damned released the first UK punk single and album. They later moved into gothic and psychedelic rock, helping shape goth.
know: Their single New Rose (1976) is often cited as the first British punk single.
They were the first UK punk band to tour the United States, playing CBGB in 1977.
Guitarist Captain Sensible later scored a UK number one as a solo artist with Happy Talk in 1982.

influencedBy.why: They covered the Stooges on their debut and borrowed their blunt, fast attack.
The band covered the MC5 and shared their high-energy garage approach.
The Dolls' trashy glam-punk was a clear model for the early Damned.
Nick Lowe produced their debut album for Stiff Records.
Pink Floyd drummer Nick Mason produced their second album, Music for Pleasure.

influenced.why: Guns N' Roses covered New Rose on The Spaghetti Incident?.
The Damned's horror imagery and dark theatrics anticipated the Misfits' horror punk.

cousins.why: Lemmy briefly played with members of the Damned, and both bands share a loud, fast, no-frills drive.
Same mix of theatrical horror imagery and hard-hitting rock.

summary: Art-school band whose terse, minimalist songs pushed punk toward post-punk. Their first three albums are touchstones for generations of indie and punk bands.
know: Their debut Pink Flag packs 21 songs into about 35 minutes.
R.E.M. covered their song Strange on the album Document.
The band was formed by art students, and that background shows in their abstract lyrics and structures.

influencedBy.why: Wire took the Ramones' brevity and stripped it down even further.
Their drone and art-world approach echo the Velvet Underground.
Eno's art-school experimentalism parallels Wire's move into texture on Chairs Missing and 154.

influenced.why: R.E.M. covered Wire's Strange on Document.
Minor Threat covered Wire's 12XU.
Big Black covered Wire's Heartbeat and shared their clipped, angular style.
Elastica's Connection drew directly on the riff of Three Girl Rhumba.
Blur's members have cited Wire, and their angular guitar shows on Modern Life Is Rubbish era songs.
Bloc Party's jagged post-punk revival guitar draws on Wire's template.
Franz Ferdinand's tight, angular songs follow the Wire model.

cousins.why: Both reduced music to precise, minimal parts.
Same art-minded willingness to rebuild rock from repetition and texture.

summary: Mark E. Smith's long-running band, built on repetitive, abrasive grooves and his sardonic spoken-sung delivery. With dozens of lineup changes, they released more than 30 studio albums.
know: Mark E. Smith was the only constant member through dozens of lineup changes.
They recorded 24 sessions for John Peel, who called them his favorite band.
Guitarist Brix Smith joined in 1983 and brought a poppier edge to their mid-1980s albums.
keyAlbums: The Wonderful and Frightening World of The Fall

influencedBy.why: Smith wrote I Am Damo Suzuki as a tribute to Can's singer, and Can's repetition runs through the band.
The Velvets' drone and repetition are a documented root of the Fall's sound.
Smith admired Beefheart, whose skewed rhythms and wordplay echo through the Fall.
Their primitive garage drive owes a debt to the Stooges.

influenced.why: Pavement's slack, cryptic indie rock is widely traced to the Fall.
Sonic Youth recorded an EP of Fall covers, 4 Tunna Brix.
James Murphy's talk-sung delivery over repetitive grooves follows the Fall's lead.
Fontaines D.C.'s deadpan vocals over driving post-punk echo the Fall.
Manchester's later bands, including Happy Mondays, inherited the Fall's loose, sardonic style.

cousins.why: Both deliver wry, conversational vocals rooted in everyday English life.
Same love of strange characters, odd words and rough-edged delivery.

summary: Leeds band that merged punk's sharpness with funk rhythms and politically minded lyrics. Their debut Entertainment! became a blueprint for dance-punk.
know: Andy Gill's choppy, trebly guitar left gaps for the bass and drums to carry the groove.
The founding members met as students at the University of Leeds.
Andy Gill produced the Red Hot Chili Peppers' debut album in 1984.
songs: I Love a Man in a Uniform

influencedBy.why: Funk was central to their rhythm section, and they took cues from Funkadelic's grooves.
Their interlocking, rhythm-first arrangements recall James Brown's funk.
Dub's use of space and dropouts shaped their sparse mixes.
The Pistols' arrival gave the Leeds students the push to form a band.

influenced.why: Andy Gill produced the Chili Peppers' debut album.
Michael Stipe has named Gang of Four as an important early influence.
Kurt Cobain listed Entertainment! among his favorite albums.
Franz Ferdinand's angular dance rock is widely traced to Gang of Four.
LCD Soundsystem's dance-punk follows the Gang of Four template.
Bloc Party's spiky guitar and danceable drums draw on Entertainment!.
Fugazi's tense, funk-inflected post-hardcore echoes Gang of Four.

cousins.why: Both built songs around tight, choppy rhythm guitar and bass.
Same fusion of hard groove and political message.

summary: John Lydon's band after the Sex Pistols, built on dub bass, abrasive guitar and long, hypnotic songs. Metal Box is one of post-punk's defining records.

Jah Wobble's deep, dub-style bass anchored the early lineup alongside Keith Levene's guitar.
Album (1986) was produced by Bill Laswell and featured Steve Vai and Ginger Baker.
songs: This Is Not a Love Song

influencedBy.why: PiL was Lydon's next step after leaving the Sex Pistols.
Lydon and the band admired Can, whose long, repetitive grooves shaped Metal Box.
Lydon has named Beefheart as a favorite, and his skewed approach shows in PiL.
PiL's heavy, spacious bass sound grew from the band's love of dub.
Lydon has cited Peter Hammill of Van der Graaf Generator as an influence on his singing.

influenced.why: Faith No More's Bill Gould has cited PiL's bass-heavy sound.
LCD Soundsystem's long, bass-driven dance-punk grooves follow PiL.

cousins.why: Both built dark, bass-heavy music out of dub.
Same interest in pushing dub into post-punk territory.

summary: London punk band fronted by Poly Styrene, whose sharp songs about consumerism and identity stood out in 1977. Their one album of the era is a punk classic.

songs: The Day the World Turned Day-Glo

influencedBy.why: Poly Styrene decided to form a band after seeing the Sex Pistols play in 1976.
Patti Smith opened the door for a woman to lead a punk band on her own terms.
Roxy Music had already put saxophone into art-minded rock.

influenced.why: Riot grrrl bands like Bikini Kill cited Poly Styrene as a model.
Sleater-Kinney's sharp, woman-led punk follows the path X-Ray Spex opened.

cousins.why: Both were young British women with singular, unconventional voices in the late 1970s.
Same sharp social commentary set to energetic British music.

summary: All-woman London band that mixed punk with reggae and dub. Their album Cut is one of post-punk's most original records.

Cut was produced by reggae producer Dennis Bovell.
They toured with the Clash on the 1977 White Riot tour.

influencedBy.why: The Slits toured with the Clash and came up in the same London punk circle.
The Pistols' early shows set off the London scene the Slits came out of.
Their open, echoing rhythms draw on Perry's dub production.

influenced.why: Riot grrrl bands cited the Slits as a model for women making punk on their own terms.
Sleater-Kinney follows the Slits' path of fierce, woman-led punk.

cousins.why: Both were part of the British meeting of punk and reggae, and both worked with Dennis Bovell.
Same playful, untrained vocal freedom and genre mixing.

summary: Cleveland band led by David Thomas that mixed garage rock with synthesizer noise and odd song structures. Their early records helped invent post-punk before the term existed.

Allen Ravenstine's synthesizer added noise and texture rather than melody.

influencedBy.why: Beefheart's fractured rhythms and voice are a documented root of Pere Ubu.
The Velvets' noise and art-rock attitude shaped the band.

influenced.why: Black Francis has named Pere Ubu as a favorite band.
Joy Division's bleak, industrial post-punk followed early Pere Ubu.

cousins.why: Both used raw electronics as noise inside rock.
Same strange, theatrical vocal style and junkyard textures.

summary: New York duo of singer Alan Vega and keyboardist Martin Rev who made stark, repetitive rock with only cheap keyboards and a drum machine. They were a key link between punk and electronic music.

influencedBy.why: Vega said seeing the Stooges perform pushed him to make music.

The Jesus and Mary Chain cited Suicide's mix of noise and simple pop.
Ric Ocasek championed the band and produced their second album.
Depeche Mode's synth-driven rock follows Suicide's lead.
LCD Soundsystem's electronic punk draws on Suicide's minimal pulse.

cousins.why: Both stripped music down to machines and voice.
Same abrasive, minimal electronics under a shouted vocal.

summary: Richard Hell's band in the first wave of New York punk, known for Blank Generation and Robert Quine's jagged guitar. Hell's look and attitude helped define what punk would become.

summary: Derry band whose short, catchy songs about teenage life made them one of punk's great pop groups. Teenage Kicks is among the most loved singles of the era.

cousins.why: Both wrote catchy, guitar-driven power pop.
Same short, hook-filled guitar pop.

summary: Belfast punk band whose songs addressed life during the Troubles. Their debut Inflammable Material is a landmark of independent punk.

cousins.why: Both were Irish bands writing urgent rock about the conflict around them.
Same pointed songs about life in a divided Britain.

summary: Paul Weller's trio brought 1960s mod style into the punk era and wrote sharp songs about British life. They were one of the most popular UK bands of their time.

The Libertines' scrappy, very English guitar rock follows the Jam.

cousins.why: Both wrote energetic songs about British working-class life.
Same close-up observation of ordinary English life.

summary: Howard Devoto's band after leaving Buzzcocks, mixing punk energy with keyboards and art-rock ambition. Their debut single Shot by Both Sides is a post-punk landmark.

Same dark, keyboard-heavy moodiness.

summary: Chaotic early Los Angeles punk band fronted by Darby Crash, with guitarist Pat Smear. Their only album, GI, is a cornerstone of West Coast hardcore.

They appear in Penelope Spheeris's 1981 documentary The Decline of Western Civilization.

influencedBy.why: The Stooges' wild, raw rock was a key model for the band.

The Ramones' speed and simplicity fed the early Germs.
Joan Jett produced their album GI.

Pat Smear became a longtime Foo Fighters guitarist.

Same primitive, overdriven rock energy.

summary: Los Angeles punk band built around the twin voices of Exene Cervenka and John Doe and Billy Zoom's rockabilly guitar. They brought country and early rock and roll into punk.

Billy Zoom's guitar draws on Sun-era rockabilly like Carl Perkins.

summary: South Bay band that mixed hardcore speed with catchy melodies and songs about everyday frustration. They are one of the main roots of pop punk.

blink-182 have cited the Descendents as a key influence.

summary: Los Angeles hardcore band formed by Black Flag's first singer, Keith Morris. Their fast, short songs helped define the early California hardcore sound.

summary: Washington, D.C. band formed by Ian MacKaye and Guy Picciotto, known for tense, dynamic songs and a strict independent ethic. They are the central band of post-hardcore.

summary: New York hardcore band known for upbeat, positive songs and catchy melodies. Their album Start Today is a youth crew classic.

summary: Melbourne band fronted by Nick Cave that made ferocious, blues-twisted noise. They were a key bridge between post-punk and goth.
